name: Cocteau Twins
label: 4AD
lede: A guitarist with a box of effects pedals and a singer who wouldn't sing words people could make out left a refinery town in Scotland and gave 4AD its sound for the next decade.

eras.title: Out of Grangemouth by phone box
eras.text: Robin Guthrie and Will Heggie started the band in Grangemouth, a refinery town between Glasgow and Edinburgh, and took the name from an early Simple Minds song. Guthrie found a singer dancing at a punk night, hand-carried a cassette to London, and within a year 4AD had them in a studio.

years.src: AllMusic · Wikipedia: Robin Guthrie
years.h: Robin Guthrie and Will Heggie start a band in Grangemouth
years.p: Guthrie, a trained electrician who tinkered with fuzz boxes and pedals, and bassist Heggie name it after an obscure Simple Minds song.

years.src: cocteautwins.com: We shall both die in your rosary · Wikipedia: Elizabeth Fraser
years.h: Guthrie spots Elizabeth Fraser dancing to the Birthday Party
years.p: [[Elizabeth Fraser|0bf0cabe-def2-4113-8dc5-6e721b9c3a92]], 17, is dancing at punk nights at the Nash, the Hotel International disco where Guthrie sometimes DJs, to records nobody else will dance to. He tells her she could sing.
years.xp:
"Liz was insanely shy," Guthrie has said, but she'd sung since she was a child. She left for about six months for lack of confidence, then came back once she and Guthrie became a couple.

A friend of hers, Carol, sang with them for about two weeks; the Garlands inner sleeve carries a note to her. A drummer, John Murphy, lasted until he asked for travel expenses. Guthrie bought a drum machine.

years.cap: Will Heggie, Elizabeth Fraser and Robin Guthrie, the original trio
years.src: cocteautwins.com: We shall both die in your rosary · AllMusic
years.h: A phone box number, a tape for Ivo and a tape for John Peel
years.p: Guthrie gets 4AD's address from [[The Birthday Party|cbcd4d49-e892-4fc6-a313-35f275a153d2]]'s drummer Phill Calvert backstage, then hand-delivers demos to [[Ivo Watts-Russell|cf86cec1-1baf-4d8a-ba1e-01568332585a]] and [[John Peel|e4dec348-ad10-43b6-a2b1-c22aab890675]]. Ivo's answer: come and make a record.
years.xp:
The band had no phone. "I wrote down the number of the phone box down the road," Guthrie said, and he waited there between five and six every evening. Peel sent a supportive letter.

On the cassette Fraser's voice was buried in noise, so Watts-Russell hadn't really heard her. Once he did, in the studio, a single became a whole album.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cocteau Twins · cocteautwins.com: We shall both die in your rosary
years.h: The first John Peel session includes 'Wax and Wane'
years.p: Four songs for Peel's BBC show, among them 'Wax and Wane' and 'Garlands'. It's the first of many Peel sessions.

years.src: Wikipedia: Garlands · cocteautwins.com: We shall both die in your rosary · Wikipedia: Cocteau Twins
years.h: Garlands, cut in seven days at Blackwing
years.p: Recorded at Blackwing Studios in London, produced by the band and Watts-Russell. It climbs to No. 14 on the UK indie albums chart.
years.xp:
Guthrie wanted the drum machine run through fuzz pedals and amps; the engineers wouldn't have it. "They wouldn't let us touch any of their stuff," he recalled, so the drums came out clean.

Sounds heard [[Siouxsie and the Banshees|78ea5ea1-3c4d-4b7e-ac5d-68900319ebe2]] and [[Joy Division|9a58fda3-f4ed-4080-a3a5-f457aac9fcdd]] in it. Gordon Sharp of Cindytalk sings backing vocals on three tracks.

eras.title: Down to two, and a siren song
eras.text: Heggie left in the spring and the band carried on as Guthrie and Fraser. The record that made Fraser's name that year wasn't even a Cocteau Twins record.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cocteau Twins · Wikipedia: Lowlife
years.h: Heggie quits after a Hamburg show opening for OMD
years.p: The Peppermint Pig EP is out; Heggie leaves after a gig in Hamburg supporting Orchestral Manoeuvres in the Dark. He joins Dead Neighbours, soon renamed Lowlife.

years.cap: Elizabeth Fraser and Robin Guthrie, c. 1983
years.src: Wikipedia: Song to the Siren · Wikipedia: Cocteau Twins
yt: This Mortal Coil, "Song to the Siren"
years.h: Fraser and Guthrie record 'Song to the Siren' for This Mortal Coil
years.p: Watts-Russell's 4AD collective releases its version of the Tim Buckley song with Fraser singing over Guthrie's guitar. It reaches No. 3 on the UK indie chart and stays on it for 101 weeks.
years.xp:
David Lynch wanted it for Blue Velvet in 1986, couldn't afford the licence, and had Angelo Badalamenti write 'Mysteries of Love' instead. He finally used it in Lost Highway in 1997.

Through [[This Mortal Coil|60ef8ddb-7676-4056-a357-9a8c228d03a6]], Fraser and Guthrie also met [[Simon Raymonde|54cf21b1-9a02-4a75-a029-3a66db21c545]].

years.src: Wikipedia: Head over Heels
years.h: Head over Heels: the duo record John Peel played start to finish
years.p: Made by Guthrie and Fraser at Palladium Studios in Edinburgh. NME found it hollow; Peel played the whole album on air.
years.xp: "Little of it was really planned, the songs just came together very naturally," Guthrie said. It came out alongside the Sunburst and Snowblind EP and made No. 7 in Sounds' records of 1983.

years.src: Wikipedia: Simon Raymonde · AllMusic
years.h: Simon Raymonde, son of a Dusty Springfield arranger, joins
years.p: Raymonde, ex-Drowning Craze and son of arranger Ivor Raymonde, comes in on bass after the This Mortal Coil sessions and becomes a core writer.

eras.title: No to Top of the Pops
eras.text: With Raymonde in, the band hit a run of EPs and albums that set the 4AD look and sound. They had a chart single and still wouldn't mime on the BBC, and they made a record with the ambient composer Harold Budd.

years.src: cocteautwins.com: Searching for Treasure
years.h: First US shows, in New York and Philadelphia, as a duo
years.p: Guthrie and Fraser play America for the first time; they're the last shows as a two-piece. Raymonde is in for everything after.

years.src: Wikipedia: Pearly-Dewdrops' Drops
years.h: 'Pearly-Dewdrops' Drops' hits No. 29 and tops the indie chart
years.p: The lead track of The Spangle Maker EP becomes the band's biggest UK single. John Scarlett-Davis shoots the video in a chapel at Holloway Sanatorium.

q: We couldn't do it! We physically couldn't do it.
years.src: cocteautwins.com: Searching for Treasure
years.h: Guthrie turns down Top of the Pops, twice
years.p: With a single in the chart, the band twice says no to the BBC's chart show rather than mime on its stage.
years.xp:
Guthrie couldn't see himself getting up on a stage "full of balloons and dancing girls and flashing lights" to mime to his own record.

The BBC didn't get easier. A January 1985 Old Grey Whistle Test performance of 'Lorelei' ended in a row over the sound. "Robin... was never going to back down, and I respected him for that," Raymonde said.

years.src: Wikipedia: Treasure · cocteautwins.com: Searching for Treasure
years.h: Treasure opens with a song called 'Ivo'
years.p: Ten songs named like people, starting with one for their label boss. It's the first UK Top 40 album; the band thought it underdeveloped.
years.xp:
Guthrie produced it at Palladium in Edinburgh and Rooster in West London over August and September. [[Robert Smith|7d1a1624-784b-4f89-8ff9-b9b493cd059d]] of [[The Cure|69ee3720-a7cb-4402-b48d-a02c366f2bcf]] called it "the most romantic sound I'd ever heard" and played it on his wedding day.

Fraser said the names were a joke on listeners, who would assume mythology; they had nothing to do with it.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cocteau Twins · AllMusic
years.h: Aikea-Guinea, Tiny Dynamine, Echoes in a Shallow Bay
years.p: Three EPs in one year. 4AD signs a deal with Relativity to get them into American shops.

years.cap: Cocteau Twins in the Los Angeles Times, September 7, 1985
years.src: cocteautwins.com: Searching for Treasure
years.h: Japan, where Treasure sells best, gets its first tour
years.p: The band tours Japan for the first time, where Treasure is their best seller, and goes on to US dates.
years.xp: Fraser's verdict on Japan, as the band's history site prints it: "facken' hell!"

years.src: Wikipedia: Victorialand · Wikipedia: Cocteau Twins
years.h: Victorialand is cut to vinyl at 45 rpm
years.p: Raymonde was busy with This Mortal Coil, so Guthrie and Fraser made a near-acoustic album with almost no drums or bass. It's their first UK top ten.
years.xp: The title is the Antarctic territory; several song titles come from David Attenborough's 1984 book The Living Planet. Mastering trouble with the sparse sound put the first UK pressing at 45 rpm.

years.cap: Cocteau Twins publicity photo for The Moon and the Melodies, 1986
years.src: Wikipedia: The Moon and the Melodies
years.h: Harold Budd records with them under four names, not one
years.p: The Moon and the Melodies is credited to Budd, Fraser, Guthrie and Raymonde. It began as a TV series about cross-genre collaboration that never got made.

eras.title: Capitol, a baby and Las Vegas
eras.text: An American major finally put them on US radio, and the band made its biggest record while its founder couple had a daughter and Guthrie's drug use worsened. Then they left 4AD.

years.src: Wikipedia: Blue Bell Knoll · Wikipedia: Cocteau Twins
years.h: Blue Bell Knoll, named after a peak in Utah
years.p: Capitol Records takes the band to America while 4AD keeps them at home. 'Carolyn's Fingers' reaches No. 2 on Billboard's Modern Rock chart.
years.xp: "Blue Bell Knoll was the easiest I've ever done to make a record," Fraser said, singing in her own invented language throughout. Raymonde remembered lots of joy around it.

years.src: Wikipedia: Heaven or Las Vegas · Wikipedia: Elizabeth Fraser
years.h: Fraser and Guthrie's daughter, Lucy Belle, is born
years.p: The couple's first child arrives in the middle of the sessions for the next album.

years.src: Wikipedia: Heaven or Las Vegas
years.h: Raymonde's father dies during the Heaven or Las Vegas sessions
years.p: At September Sound in Twickenham, Ivor Raymonde dies mid-album, and Guthrie is struggling with cocaine.
years.xp:
"I was only 27... that was a big blow," Raymonde said of his father. Wikipedia reports Guthrie's paranoia and mood swings strained his relationship with Fraser.

Fraser found a new confidence while pregnant, she said, which she then lost after the birth. Raymonde, recording her vocals, would "scrape the tears away and say, 'That was alright, Liz'."

years.src: Wikipedia: Heaven or Las Vegas
years.h: Heaven or Las Vegas comes out on Lucy Belle's first birthday
years.p: It goes to No. 7 in the UK, their highest, after 'Iceblink Luck' leads it out in August.
years.xp: Wikipedia counts 235,000 copies sold by 1996. Rolling Stone put it at No. 245 of its 500 greatest albums in 2020.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cocteau Twins · Wikipedia: Heaven or Las Vegas
years.h: The band leaves 4AD after eight years
years.p: Heaven or Las Vegas is their last 4AD album. Wikipedia puts it down partly to conflict with Watts-Russell and partly to problems around Guthrie's substance use.

eras.title: Splitting up and staying a band
eras.text: Fraser and Guthrie ended their 13-year relationship in 1993 and kept making records together on a new label. Guthrie got sober, the band played American TV, and it all came apart while they were working on a ninth album.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cocteau Twins · Wikipedia: Four-Calendar Café · Wikipedia: Elizabeth Fraser
years.h: Fraser and Guthrie separate, and the band signs to Fontana
years.p: The couple splits after 13 years. Mercury's Fontana takes the band in the UK, with Capitol staying on in the US.
years.xp: Guthrie went to rehab and quit alcohol and drugs; Fraser went into psychotherapy. The two kept working together through the band's contracts.

years.src: Wikipedia: Four-Calendar Café
years.h: Four-Calendar Café: every word in English, and audible
years.p: Their first album after the split, and their most direct. It's their best US chart showing, No. 78 on the Billboard 200.
years.xp: "I've consciously been stripping things back," Guthrie said. Fraser called the all-English, all-audible singing extreme. Pitchfork later wrote it is "full of trauma's echoes."

years.src: Wikipedia: Cocteau Twins · Wikipedia: Four-Calendar Café
years.h: 'Bluebeard' on Jay Leno is their first American TV
years.p: Fourteen years in, the band makes its US television debut on The Tonight Show.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cocteau Twins
years.h: NME hears Otherness as Cocteau Twins gone ambient
years.p: One of two EPs that year, with Twinlights. The NME review said it never finds a point.

years.src: Wikipedia: Milk & Kisses · Wikipedia: Cocteau Twins
years.h: Milk & Kisses, recorded in Brittany and Twickenham
years.p: The eighth album, made in two months at Pors Poulhan and September Sound, with 'Tishbite' and 'Violaine' as singles. A bigger touring band, with an extra guitarist and drummer, takes it on the road.
years.xp: The title came from a friend's comfort to Fraser: she wished she could take the pain out and replace it with milk and kisses. "It all happened so fast," Raymonde said; Guthrie called it a joyous experience.

q: It's not lost, it's upstairs on my computer.
years.src: cocteautwins.com: FAQ · Wikipedia: Cocteau Twins · Wikipedia: Elizabeth Fraser
years.h: The band breaks up during the ninth album
years.p: The trio splits over what Wikipedia calls irreconcilable differences, tied partly to Fraser and Guthrie's breakup. The new songs stay unfinished.
years.xp:
Guthrie says the material was only sketches. Finished instrumentals turned up on his solo album Imperial and in Violet Indiana.

In 2009 Fraser told the Guardian she couldn't bear sharing a stage with Guthrie. Of the band, she said: "they were my life."

years.src: Wikipedia: Cocteau Twins · Wikipedia: Simon Raymonde
years.h: Raymonde and Guthrie start Bella Union
years.p: The label's first release is Raymonde's solo album Blame Someone Else. Raymonde later signs [[Fleet Foxes|fa97dd36-1b82-43d7-a6e4-2adeafd59cef]], [[Midlake|da90b5da-349e-4906-a0b4-805f5e46190d]] and [[John Grant|27ca9c68-650a-4659-b8ef-013e5698ff55]].

eras.title: Teardrop, Coachella and a closed door
eras.text: Fraser's voice reached its biggest audience on someone else's record. A reunion got as far as a festival booking before she pulled out, and the band has said since it won't come back.

years.src: Wikipedia: Teardrop · Wikipedia: Elizabeth Fraser
years.h: Massive Attack pick Fraser over Madonna for 'Teardrop'
years.p: Fraser writes the words and sings the second single from Mezzanine. It's [[Massive Attack|10adbe5e-a2c0-4bf3-8249-2b4cbf6e6ca8]]'s biggest UK hit, No. 10.
years.xp: She recorded it in 1997 as news came of [[Jeff Buckley|e6e879c0-3d56-4f12-b3c5-3ce459661a8e]]'s drowning; they had been close. "That song's kind of about him," Fraser said.

years.cap: Elizabeth Fraser singing "Teardrop" with Massive Attack
years.src: Wikipedia: Cocteau Twins · Wikipedia: Elizabeth Fraser
years.h: Fraser pulls out, and the Coachella reunion is off
years.p: The band had announced a reunion for Coachella on April 30. Raymonde later said a 55-date world tour was booked that would have paid him £1.5 million.
years.xp: In 2009 Fraser said she didn't remember it being that much money, "and in any case that's not the reason." In 2021 Raymonde said the band would never reform to play or record.

years.src: Wikipedia: Elizabeth Fraser · Wikipedia: Cocteau Twins
years.h: Fraser's first shows in 14 years, at Meltdown
years.p: Two nights at the Royal Festival Hall, with Cocteau Twins songs in new arrangements. She called singing them an endurance test.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cocteau Twins · Wikipedia: Elizabeth Fraser
years.h: The Ivors Academy gives the trio its Visionary Award
years.p: Fraser and Guthrie collect it in London. A month later Fraser and partner Damon Reece put out the Sun's Signature EP.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cocteau Twins
years.h: Guthrie remasters the two Fontana albums for 4AD
years.p: Four-Calendar Café and Milk & Kisses come back on 4AD, and Raymonde publishes his memoir, In One Ear.
